mode: self-review (nested sub-agent spawning restricted in this environment)
summary: MESSAGE composer branch is well-structured: single outer try/catch preserves per-node at-most-once + lost-forward semantics, shared renderTrimmed helper removes the 6x trim duplication, per-block dispatch is exhaustive over BlockType (no default), keyboard anchored to last non-album block via a single reverse scan. Catch-arm order/mapping matches the former flat branches exactly. Cross-file signatures verified against Task 2 TelegramSender (sendVideo/Audio/Document 6-arg, sendMediaGroup 4-arg) and Task 1 model (ContentBlock/MediaItem/BlockType).

findings.finding: buildAlbum javadoc referenced a removed helper name 'albumElementType' after it was inlined to the ALBUM_ELEMENT_TYPE constant.
findings.resolution: Updated the comment to reference the ALBUM_ELEMENT_TYPE constant + its declared rationale.

findings.finding: If a step has buttons but every block is an album (lastNonAlbumIndex == -1), no block receives the keyboard yet the branch still returns WAIT_FOR_REPLY, parking on a reply that can never arrive (until timeout). This is an invalid step shape.
findings.reason: Task 3 spec explicitly says NOT to invent runtime behavior for 'buttons + last block album' — that shape is rejected at save (422) by Task 4 validation, so the executor never sees it in practice. Keeping park/cont anchored to the last non-album block matches the spec's stated contract. Documented as a known validation-enforced precondition.

findings.finding: ALBUM_ELEMENT_TYPE hardcoded to 'photo' because the Task 1 model carries no per-item media type (MediaItem is url+caption only, ContentBlock.type is the single ALBUM discriminator).
findings.reason: Model limitation from Task 1 — photo+video album mixing (Decision 5) is not expressible until the model carries an element-type hint. Recorded in decisions.md Deviations.

verification: Isolated javac of all main sources (StepExecutor + Task1 model + Task2 sender) = 0 errors; FunnelStepExecutorTest 24/24 green via JUnit launcher; both test files compile in isolation against the test classpath.
